title: Bram and the Tide
premise: Orsen Thackeray, a widowed single father running Saltmere's last bookshop, agrees to a fake date with Bram Vale — the tide-pool researcher renting his back room — to survive his family's reunion, where an inheritance dispute over the shop threatens to evict them both. The fake romance deepens into something real just as Orsen's aunt files papers to sell the building, forcing Orsen to choose between proving he's 'stable' for custody of his daughter and admitting what he actually wants. When Bram's research grant ends and her train home approaches, Orsen finally lets someone stay: he publicly claims both the shop and Bram, and the family, moved by his honesty, gifts him the deed. The book ends one year later, with the reunion held in the bookshop and no one pretending anything.
about_author: August Marchetti is the pen name of a former coastal bookseller who spent a decade shelving romances in a shop that smelled of salt and old paper. They write love stories about people who arrive late but stay long.

chapters.title: The Last Train Schedule
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen juggles his daughter Wren's school forms, a dwindling till, and a letter summoning him to the Thackeray family reunion, where Aunt Cordelia plans to discuss 'the future of the property.' He notices his lodger Bram reading tide charts on the shop floor and feels the first flicker of curiosity. Emotional beat: quiet dread softened by unexpected warmth.

chapters.title: A Reasonable Fiction
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram, whose grant ends in eight weeks, overhears Orsen dreading the reunion's interrogation about his love life and impulsively offers to pose as his partner. They negotiate terms over burnt coffee: hand-holding allowed, feelings forbidden. Emotional beat: playful bravado masking two lonely people's mutual recognition.

chapters.title: Reunion at Gullwing House
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The fake couple arrives at the family estate; Cordelia probes their story while cousin Felix needles Orsen about being 'the brother who stayed behind.' Wren, sharp-eyed, nearly exposes them by asking why Papa never holds hands like that. Emotional beat: performance turning perilously easy.

chapters.title: Dessert and Other Confessions
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Over dessert, Cordelia announces she'll sell the bookshop building unless Orsen demonstrates 'a stable household' within six weeks. Walking home along the seawall, Orsen and Bram drop the act without meaning to, sharing real stories under a rising moon. Emotional beat: the fake date becomes true by accident.

chapters.title: What the Tide Leaves Behind
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram surveys tide pools with Wren in tow, and the girl asks if she's staying forever. Bram deflects, unsettled by how much she wants to say yes. She finds her grant renewal denied and hides the letter in a tide chart. Emotional beat: hope curdling into countdown.

chapters.title: Six Weeks of Almost
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A montage of domestic near-misses: shared dinners, Wren's school play where they sit together like a family, a kiss interrupted by a customer. Orsen starts renovating the shop to prove stability; Bram quietly packs. Emotional beat: tenderness built on an unspoken expiration date.

chapters.title: The Letter in the Tide Chart
chapters.summary: Wren's POV (child narrator). Wren finds Bram's denial letter and, not fully understanding, shows it to Cordelia at tea, hoping to help Bram stay. Cordelia sees leverage instead. Emotional beat: innocence triggering catastrophe.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Cordelia confronts Orsen: his 'stable household' is a fiction and his partner is leaving; sign the sale or lose everything. Orsen, humiliated that Bram hid the letter, says things he can't take back. Bram leaves for the station hotel. Emotional beat: the lie's collapse wounding what was real.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. At the empty platform, Bram realizes every reason to leave is a reason born of fear. She returns through rain to find Orsen closing the shop and tells him the truth: she was afraid of wanting to stay. Orsen chooses her over pride. Emotional beat: raw, rain-soaked confession as climax.

chapters.title: Everything Worth Keeping
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the family gathering, Orsen refuses to perform stability and instead speaks plainly about grief, fatherhood, and Bram — moving even Cordelia, who tears up the sale papers and deeds him the shop. Epilogue one year later: the reunion is held among the bookshelves, Wren teaching cousins tide pooling, nothing pretended. Emotional beat: belonging earned, inheritance redefined.
